title: Organize and find your notes
p: Your documents should stay easy to explore as their number grows. Group related notes under a parent document, pins and favorites to keep useful pages close, and links and search to find connections.
Click Home in the sidebar or press ⌘ ⌥ Home to see your documents.

ul.li: My documents and Favorites: My documents shows top-level documents. Favorites shows the documents you have marked.
Sort: choose last opened, last modified, creation time or title. Your choice is remembered.
Right-click a row or use its More menu for document actions.

p: Every document in your library can have child documents. Open a parent to edit its title and body, and use the list at the end of the page to open its children.

ul.li: Expand or collapse: click the arrow beside a parent document in the sidebar. Hold ⌥ to expand or collapse the whole branch.
Add a child: hover over a document in the sidebar and click its plus button. The New child document menu item also lets you choose Markdown.

p: Open Examples to see two child documents, Example: reading list and Example: weekly meeting. Use the path at the top of a child document to return to its parent.
Drag a sidebar entry between rows to reorder it. Drop it onto another document to make it a child. You can also drag one document onto another from Home.
Right-click a sidebar entry or click its More button.

td.p: Keep a reference next to the document you are writing.
Create an editable copy of the document and its children.
Move the document and its children under another document or back to the top level. Search for a destination in the dialog.
Place a shortcut in the sidebar's Pinned section.
Include the document in Home's Favorites tab.
Export PDF or Markdown; see Import, export and back up.
Edit the title in the sidebar. Enter confirms; Esc cancels.
Move the document and all its descendants to Trash.

p: Entries you have not arranged by hand appear first, newest first; the rest keep the order you dragged them into.
Use the batch control beside My documents, or Shift-click a document. Select up to 50 pages, then use the footer to duplicate, move or delete them together. Press Esc to leave batch mode.

callout.p: Visible at the top of the sidebar. Keep a few daily essentials here, such as your weekly plan.
Collected in their own Home tab. Useful for references you want to return to without filling the sidebar.

p: Type @ to see recently opened pages, then type a title to search. Pick a page to insert a link, such as Writing: text, headings and paragraphs. The link keeps working if the destination is renamed.
The reference area at the end of a document shows incoming and outgoing links. Incoming links include the surrounding text; click one to jump to that mention.
Both example documents mention this guide, so they appear in its backlinks. You can hide the reference area with its close button and show it again from the document's More menu.

callout.p: The tree answers “Where does this note belong?” Links answer “What is it connected to?” Use both when a note has more than one context.

p: Press ⌘ J or use the search control in the header or on Home. Search matches document titles and body text, prioritizes titles, and shows highlighted snippets.

ul.li: With an empty query, search shows recently visited documents.
Use the arrow keys to select, Enter to open and Esc to close.
You can also search selected text from the formatting toolbar's More menu.

p: Press ⌘ F to find text in the current document. Enter moves to the next match; Shift-Enter moves back. ⌘ ⇧ H opens replacement controls for one match or all matches. Search is case-insensitive.

ul.li: Outline: jump between headings and keep track of the current section. Each document remembers whether its outline is expanded.
Page width: choose the default, wide or full-width layout from the More menu. Wide layouts are useful for tables.
Reading mode: ⌃ ⌥ V makes the view read-only while keeping selection, copying and folding available. ⌃ ⌥ E returns to editing.
Document information: inspect dates, word and character counts, and file size. Words and numbers are counted as words; each CJK character is counted individually.

p: Deleting a document sends it and all its descendants to Trash. Open the parent there to read it and browse its children. Click the Trash icon at the bottom of the sidebar to get back to the list.

ul.li: Restore brings a document and the descendants deleted with it back to their original place. If the original parent is unavailable, the restored branch goes to the top level.
Trash is included in Git backup when Git is enabled, so deleting and restoring documents can be synced.
